ns2:section.sectionText: This seminar addresses two questions: 1) to what extent are human social attitudes and behaviors a function of genetic and neurophysiological causes? 2) given man's newfound ability to alter our species' genetic makeup to what extent should government regulate this special kind of research? The course inevitably calls into question the relationships among political science, law, and biology. Only a rudimentary knowledge of genetics is required. Grades will be based on class attendance, participation, and a semester research project. Instructor written permission needed for enrollment.
